PDI: Pentaho Data Integration, the ETL platform this course is built around. It reads data from sources, reshapes it, and loads it into targets using transformations and jobs.
Kettle: The original open-source name for PDI's engine. You still meet it in file extensions (.ktr, .kjb) and the kettle.properties configuration file.
Spoon: The desktop design tool where you build, preview, and run PDI transformations and jobs on a visual canvas.
Transformation: A PDI data flow made of steps connected by hops, saved as a .ktr file. It moves and reshapes rows of data and runs all its steps in parallel.
Job: A PDI orchestration unit saved as a .kjb file. It sequences transformations and other tasks, handling control flow, conditions, and success or failure paths.
Step: A single processing node on a transformation canvas. Each step reads incoming rows, does one job (read a file, look up a value, write to a table), and passes rows on.
Hop: The directional arrow connecting two steps. It carries rows from one step's output to the next step's input and acts as a buffered row queue between them.
Job Entry: A task on a job canvas, the job equivalent of a step. Entries run sequentially and can be transformations, shell scripts, file operations, mail, and more.
Row: A single record flowing through a transformation, made up of named, typed fields. Steps process rows one at a time as they stream through the hops.
Field: A single named, typed value within a row, such as a customer name or an order date. Its data type (String, Integer, Number, Date, Boolean) governs how the value is stored, compared, and formatted.
Perspective: A workspace mode in Spoon. The Data Integration perspective is the canvas where you design transformations and jobs.
Preview: Running a transformation only up to a chosen step and showing the rows that arrive there, without executing the whole flow. The fastest way to debug as you build.
Kettle Variable: A named value resolved at runtime with the ${VAR} or %%VAR%% syntax, used to avoid hardcoding paths and settings so a transformation works across environments.
kettle.properties: The configuration file (in the .kettle folder of the user's home directory) that stores global variables PDI loads at startup and makes available to every transformation and job.
Parameter: A named value declared on a transformation or job and supplied when it is run, resolved with ${name}. Parameters act like local variables and can override same-named global variables for that run.
Generate Rows: A step that outputs a fixed number of rows, optionally with static fields. Handy for test data or as a single-row starter that kicks off a transformation.
Data Grid: A step that holds a static grid of rows you type in by hand. Used for testing, reference data, and demos, with a Meta tab for field types and a Data tab for values.
Select Values: A step that selects, renames, reorders, or removes fields and changes their data types and formats. The standard way to do explicit type conversion in a flow.
Calculator: A step that adds calculated fields using a fixed menu of built-in operations such as add, multiply, and date difference. Fast and clear, but limited to those operations.
Formula: A scripting step that builds fields from spreadsheet-style expressions (IF, SUM, CONCAT and similar). Good for calculations and business logic that go beyond the Calculator.
Modified JavaScript Value: A scripting step (often shortened to MJV) that runs arbitrary per-row JavaScript. Very flexible for custom logic, but slower and harder to debug than purpose-built steps.
Text File Input: A step that reads delimited or fixed-width text files such as CSV. It handles headers, enclosures, multiple files, and wildcard file lists.
Text File Output: A step that writes rows to a delimited or fixed-width text file, with options like field formatting and splitting output into a new file every N rows.
JSON Input: A step that reads a JSON document and extracts fields using JSONPath expressions, the JSON equivalent of XPath.
Get data from XML: A step that reads an XML document and maps nodes to PDI fields using XPath expressions.
Excel Writer: A step that writes rows to an Excel spreadsheet. Its Append option controls whether rows go into an existing file and sheet or a fresh one is created.
Database Connection: The configured link to a relational database (driver, host, port, schema, credentials) that database steps share. PDI connects through JDBC drivers placed on its classpath.
Table Input: A step that runs a SQL SELECT against a database connection and emits each result row into the transformation.
Table Output: A step that inserts rows into a database table. It only inserts, so it is paired with other steps when updates are also needed.
Insert / Update: A step that performs an upsert: it looks up each row by key, updates the matching row if found, and inserts a new row if not.
Database Lookup: A step that fetches values from a database table for each incoming row based on lookup keys. With caching enabled it reads the table once and avoids repeated queries.
Database Join: A step that runs a parameterised SQL query once per incoming row, joining each row against the database. Flexible, but slower than a merge join on large datasets.
Merge Join: A step that joins two input streams that are both sorted on the join key, walking them in lockstep. Supports INNER, LEFT OUTER, RIGHT OUTER, and FULL OUTER joins.
Join Rows: A step that produces the Cartesian product of two streams, outputting every combination of rows from the two inputs.
Merge Rows (diff): A step that compares two sorted streams and flags each row as new, changed, deleted, or identical, the basis of change-data-capture patterns.
Sort Rows: A step that sorts the stream on one or more fields. Required upstream of steps like Merge Join and Group By that rely on ordered input.
Filter Rows: A step that evaluates a condition per row and routes matching rows to a true hop and non-matching rows to a false hop. Unwired hops simply discard those rows.
Slowly Changing Dimension: A dimension table whose attributes change over time. Type 1 overwrites the old value, while Type 2 keeps history by adding a new versioned row with effective-date ranges.
Dimension Lookup / Update: The step that maintains a slowly changing dimension. It can run as a read-only lookup or write changes, supporting Type 1 overwrite, Type 2 versioning, and punch-through updates.
MinIO: An S3-compatible object storage system. PDI reaches MinIO buckets through an S3 VFS connection, the same way it reaches Amazon S3.
Carte: A lightweight standalone PDI server that listens over HTTP to run transformations and jobs. It powers clustered runs as master and slave nodes.
Run Configuration: A named choice of where and how a transformation or job runs, such as Local in Spoon, on the Pentaho Server, or on a Carte cluster.
Pan and Kitchen: The command-line runners for production and scheduling. Pan runs a transformation (.ktr) and Kitchen runs a job (.kjb).
Log Level: How much detail PDI writes when running, from Nothing up to RowLevel. RowLevel is the most verbose and prints individual row values for deep debugging.
Error Handling: Per-step handling that routes failed rows down a separate error hop instead of stopping the flow. The error stream adds fields describing the error and the fields that caused it.
